analysis.investment_thesis: BlueStone scores in the bottom decile on both Magic Formula metrics — Earnings Yield of ~0.78% (EBIT ₹76 Cr / EV ~₹9,805 Cr) and ROCE of just 2.33% — making it mathematically uninvestable under the formula. Despite impressive 56.5% revenue CAGR, the company is a capital-burning pre-profitability story with deeply negative free cash flow of -₹828 Cr in FY2025.
key_strengths: Revenue compounding at 56.5% CAGR (₹461 Cr → ₹1,770 Cr), demonstrating real market traction
Operating income turned positive for first time (₹76 Cr in FY2025 vs. -₹6 Cr prior year)
High gross margin of 41.2% suggests attractive unit economics if overhead is controlled
key_risks: Free cash flow destruction accelerating: -₹828 Cr in FY2025 vs. -₹280 Cr prior year
Finance costs (₹208 Cr, CAGR 124%) now exceed EBIT (₹76 Cr), keeping net profit deeply negative at -₹222 Cr
Promoter holding dangerously low at 16.27% — minimal skin in the game from founders
red_flags: Earnings Yield ~0.78% — 15x below Magic Formula's minimum attractive threshold of 12%
ROCE of 2.33% — 8x below Magic Formula's minimum attractive threshold of 20%
Operating CF turned sharply negative: -₹666 Cr in FY2025 vs. +₹27 Cr in FY2023 — cash burn is accelerating, not shrinking
Total debt doubled in 2 years to ₹1,915 Cr while generating zero net profit
Net loss worsened to -₹222 Cr in FY2025 despite revenue growth — operating leverage is not materialising
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Running the Magic Formula: EBIT is ₹76 Cr (FY2025 operating income, first positive year), Enterprise Value is ~₹9,805 Cr (market cap ₹7,939 Cr + debt ₹1,915 Cr - cash ₹49 Cr). Earnings Yield = 0.78% — catastrophically below the 12% threshold I require. ROCE from the data is 2.33%, far below the 20%+ floor for a quality business. Both pillars of the Magic Formula fail completely, placing BlueStone in the worst decile on valuation AND capital efficiency simultaneously. The EV/EBITDA of 60.6x and P/S of 3.58x confirm the market is pricing in a decade of future perfection.

The operating trajectory is directionally correct — EBITDA improved from -₹1,222 Cr to +₹121 Cr over three years, and gross margins at 41% are respectable for a jewellery retailer. But the free cash flow story is deteriorating, not improving: -₹828 Cr in FY2025, driven by operating cash burn of -₹666 Cr. Finance costs of ₹208 Cr are now 2.7x EBIT, meaning the business is not yet earning enough to service its own debt. The low 16.27% promoter holding is a structural concern. This is a venture-stage growth story masquerading as a public market stock — interesting operationally, but the Magic Formula says wait until ROIC clears 20% and the price reflects reality.
